title: Recognising paraphrase
subtitle: Same idea, different words
summary: Spot the distractors, match what you hear to what is written even when the words change, and choose two answers from a longer list.

media.label: Track 13
media.title: Four extracts with distractors
media.caption: Each answer is mentioned - but so is at least one wrong option.

media.label: Track 14
media.title: Paraphrased options
media.caption: The words in the options never appear. Listen for the synonym instead.

media.label: Track 15
media.title: A new mobile phone
media.caption: All five options are mentioned. Only two of them are disadvantages the speaker states.

lesson.heading: Distractors are on purpose
lesson.text: For most questions you will hear **two or more** possible answers, but only one is correct. The wrong ones are called **distractors**, and they are there to check that you really understood, not just that you caught a word.

examples.note: Tuesday, Thursday and Friday are distractors.
*environment* and *pollution* are mentioned as the wider topic.

examples.text: The problem is a lack of **funds**.

lesson.note: While you listen, write down every candidate and cross out the ones the speakers rule out.

lesson.heading: The question will not use the recording's words
lesson.text: The questions **paraphrase** what you hear - they express the same idea in different words. Most often that means a **synonym**: one word swapped for another with a similar meaning.

lesson.heading: How the swap looks in a real question
rows: no - they will do it in the morning
no - they will borrow a car
lesson.note: Notice that a wrong option is usually mentioned *and then rejected*. Hearing the words is not enough - listen to what happens to them.

lesson.heading: Two orders to keep in mind

left.label: The questions
left.text: Always in the order you hear the information.
examples: You hear the answer to Q1 before the answer to Q2.
If you are lost, move on - the next answer is still ahead of you.

right.label: The options in a list
examples: In multiple choice and matching, A-E can come in any order.
Keep scanning the whole list as you listen.

lesson.heading: Choosing from a longer list
lesson.text: Sometimes you must pick two or three answers from a list of five or six. **All** of the ideas get mentioned, so underline the key words - the part of each option that makes it different from the others - before you listen.

examples.note: Rejected: *it can take very good photos*.
Rejected: it has a big screen, but it still fits in your pocket - not a disadvantage.

lesson.note: Pay close attention to negatives (*isn't*, *can't*) and to adjectives. They are usually the key words.

lesson.text: Read the question stem as carefully as the options. It tells you how many answers to choose and what kind of thing you are listening for - problems, solutions, advantages.

exercises.prompt: Match each word with the synonym you might hear in its place.
The option says *a place to stay*. Which words in the recording point to it?
exercises.explanation: *Accommodation* (or *hotel*) paraphrases *a place to stay*. The other three belong to the distractor options.

exercises.statement: In a multiple-choice question, the wrong options are usually never mentioned in the recording.
exercises.explanation: The opposite: distractors are almost always mentioned, then ruled out. That is what makes them work.

exercises.statement: The answers come in the same order as the questions on the paper.
exercises.explanation: The information you need for Question 1 comes before the information for Question 2 - so if you miss one, look forward, not back.

exercises.prompt: A list of options A-E is printed under a matching question. In what order will you hear them?
options: Only the correct ones are mentioned
exercises.explanation: Where you choose an option from a list, the options themselves come in random order - keep scanning all of them.

exercises.prompt: Five disadvantages of a phone are listed and all five are mentioned. Sort them by what the speaker actually says.

items.text: it has a short battery life

exercises.prompt: The incorrect answers to a question are called ___.
exercises.explanation: Identifying them shows you understood the recording rather than just recognised a word.

exercises.prompt: You hear *We could hire a car... no, actually Ben said we can borrow his.* The option is *car hire*. Is it correct?
options: Yes - the words *hire a car* were said
No - the idea is mentioned and then rejected
Yes - borrowing and hiring mean the same
exercises.explanation: Hearing the words is not the test. The speakers decide against hiring, so it is a distractor.

exercises.prompt: Build the instruction that tells you how many answers to choose.
exercises.answer: What TWO disadvantages does the speaker mention?
exercises.explanation: *TWO* and *disadvantages* are both key words - the number and the type of information.

exercises.prompt: A word with a similar meaning to another word is called a ___.
exercises.explanation: Building synonym pairs is the single most useful preparation for the Listening paper.
